info.title: OpenAsy Traces API
info.summary: Which service makes a request slow: OpenTelemetry traces kept in VictoriaTraces, services, endpoints, a map and any trace as a waterfall.
info.description:
Every screen of Traces uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457). Every read of spans takes a window, `start` and `end` in RFC 3339, the last hour by default.

Spans are pushed over OTLP/HTTP, protobuf or JSON, to `/opentelemetry/v1/traces` with `TRACES_INGEST_TOKEN`; a collector's otlphttp exporter takes `https://traces.example.com/opentelemetry` as its endpoint. Jaeger's query API is answered under `/jaeger` as Jaeger answers it, so Grafana takes `https://traces.example.com/jaeger` as a Jaeger data source with an API token as bearer token. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Every service that sent spans in the window, with the rate, errors and latency of the requests it answered, busiest first.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: RFC 3339; an hour before end when left out. The window may not reach back further than the retention.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: RFC 3339; now when left out.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Services, and the databases, queues and hosts they call that send no spans, with each call's rate, errors and p95. A call is a client or producer span; it goes to the service whose server or consumer span answered it, or else to what its attributes name (db.system, messaging.system, peer.service, server.address). The window may be at most 6 hours.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: RFC 3339; an hour before end when left out. The window may not reach back further than the retention.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: RFC 3339; now when left out.

parameters.description: RFC 3339; now when left out.

parameters.name: service

parameters.description: A span with this name.

parameters.name: errors
parameters.description: true: a span that failed.

parameters.name: minDurationMs
parameters.description: A span that took at least this long.

parameters.name: maxDurationMs
parameters.description: A span that took at most this long.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many traces; 20 when left out.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Traces runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Traces origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_traces_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003). Grafana sends one as its data source's bearer token.

adminToken.description: Only when Traces is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `TRACES_INGEST_TOKEN`: for OpenTelemetry SDKs and collectors. It can push spans, nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.
